title: What happens if you mix hot and cold water in space?
sources: NASA Glenn Research Center Fluid Physics

lines.text: What bizarre physics happens if you try mixing boiling hot water with ice cold water in zero gravity?
lines.caps: What happens mixing *hot | and cold water | in *space?

lines.text: On Earth, hot water naturally rises to the top because heat lowers density, driving convection currents.
lines.caps: On Earth, hot water *rises | due to natural | *convection

lines.text: In zero gravity aboard the space station, there is no up or down, meaning natural buoyancy completely disappears.
lines.caps: In zero gravity | buoyancy *does not | exist!

lines.text: When astronauts inject hot and cold water into a single floating sphere, the temperatures do not circulate.
lines.caps: Hot and cold water | form a single *floating | *sphere

lines.text: Instead of churning into warm water, heat can only transfer sluggishly through slow molecular diffusion.
You end up with a single floating liquid orb that is scalding hot on one side and freezing on the other.
lines.caps: One side stays *scalding hot | while the other is *freezing!

lines.text: In space, even simple liquids behave like strange alien substances.
